title: What happened to the lost colony at Roanoke?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the mystery of the Lost Colony of Roanoke, the English settlement on Roanoke Island, off present-day North Carolina's Outer Banks, that vanished by the time John White returned in 1590. They cover Sir Walter Ralegh's patent and the three settlement waves (the 1585 Ralph Lane expedition, the 1587 City of Raleigh colony led by John White, and the Virginia Dare birth), the hostile and friendly relations with local tribes, White's three-year delay and the discovery of the word "CROATOAN" carved on a tree and post, and the lack of distress signal. They discuss searches at Jamestown, reports of English-speaking people, theories including Lee Miller's sabotage and tribal absorption, the Lumbee connection, the Dare Stones, and a 2013 study of a historic map patch suggesting a fort site up the Albemarle Sound. The episode ends with a listener mail about a role-playing game inspired by the show.
topics: English colonization of the New World

segments.title: Opening banter and Roanoke location
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the topic and joke about the carving 'Croatoan'. Chuck confuses Roanoke, North Carolina with Roanoke, Virginia; Josh clarifies it is the Outer Banks island settled by the English.

segments.title: Ralegh's patent and first expedition
segments.summary: Sir Walter Ralegh received a patent from Queen Elizabeth I to settle the New World, restricted to non-Christian-settled land, which led to settling North Carolina. The 1585 expedition was led by Ralph Lane, a harsh leader who held Secotan leaders hostage and killed people, and the group left after ten months.

segments.title: Second expedition and John White's colony
segments.summary: After the first group returned to England, a larger colony of families was sent under governor John White, roughly 117 to 118 people. They arrived in July, late for planting, settled Roanoke, and Virginia Dare was born, the first English child born in the New World.

segments.title: White's return to England and the 1590 discovery
segments.summary: White sailed back to England for supplies and was delayed about three years by the Anglo-Spanish war. When he returned in 1590 the settlement was empty, with no bodies or signs of a massacre, only a fort or palisade. The word CROATOAN was carved on a tree and post, not the agreed Maltese cross distress signal.

segments.title: Searches and reports from Jamestown
segments.summary: No expedition searched for the colonists until Jamestown in 1607. Jamestown planners questioned local Indians, who reported English-style stone houses, English-speaking people who read the Bible, and a blond boy and gray-eyed people in Native clothing.

segments.title: Search challenges and theories of absorption and Lumbee link
segments.summary: The exact site of the settlement was unknown due to poor records, and erosion may have put it underwater. Theories include assimilation into a friendly tribe fifty miles inland and a link to the Lumbee tribe, whose members had surnames matching colonists by 1719.

segments.title: Sabotage theory, Fernandez, and the Dare Stones
segments.summary: Lee Miller proposed that rivals of Ralegh sabotaged the colony; pilot Fernandez stranded them late in the season and a Spanish-connected figure, Francis Walsingham, is implicated. Miller also suggests the colonists were caught in tribal power shifts and sold into slavery. The Dare Stones, forty etched granite stones found from North Carolina to near Atlanta, are considered mostly fakes, though Brown University is reevaluating them.

segments.title: 2013 map patch and possible fort site
segments.summary: The First Colony Foundation and the British Museum examined a John White map and found patches; one hidden beneath a patch appears to show a fort near the confluence of the Chowan and Roanoke rivers up Albemarle Sound. The site may be under a subdivision and golf course. The hosts note the findings are not conclusive.

segments.title: Listener mail: Dungeons and Dragons-style game
segments.summary: Listener Matt McCulley, a math teacher, describes a role-playing game he created inspired by the show, set on a college campus.

segments.title: Outro and sponsor
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener feedback and mention the website, then a sponsor credit closes the episode.
